content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm working on linking six [product_name] devices together to set up a SCADA-style system. Five devices run separate programs, while the sixth gathers their data and displays it on an HMI panel. Data communication from the five devices to the main one with the HMI is functioning as intended, but I haven't figured out how the main device can send information back to the individual ones. Specifically, I want to transmit a counter value back to each device. Does anyone know how to set up VM mapping to send data back to the individual modules?

I've attached an example showing how to transmit a counter value from one [product_name] device to another using the 'Parameter VM Mapping' feature. The counter value is a DWord. Please note, this example only works on actual hardware, not in simulation.
Thank you. Is there a way to achieve this without relying on a networked program? Currently, I have separate programs on each module, with an S7Server connection established.
Are you referring to a connection between [product_name] devices using an S7Server connection?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are configuring several [product_name] devices in a SCADA-like architecture where a central module communicates with others via an HMI interface. Although successful communication from individual modules to the main one is achieved, sending data in the opposite direction presents difficulties, especially when attempting to use VM mapping. There is uncertainty regarding the networking setup, including S7Server connections and whether an integrated networked program is necessary.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope for a simple method to transmit data, like a counter value, from the central module back to individual devices without needing a fully integrated networked program. They expect straightforward configuration for two-way communication between modules.
